clips.text_en_c1: In structural engineering, the notion of a continuous load path is arguably the most fundamental principle governing safe design, irrespective of whether the members in question are beams, columns, or reinforced concrete elements. The exam revisits how loads traverse from slab through beam to column and ultimately to foundation, since failure at any single link compromises the entire structural frame.
clips.text_en_c2: The foundational principle underpinning any coherent structural assessment is that the load path must remain unequivocally continuous, traversing uninterrupted from the suspended slab through the primary beam, thence to the column, and ultimately dissipating into the foundation stratum. Should any single link within this hierarchical chain prove deficient, the consequence is not localised distress but progressive collapse of the lateral frame, a failure mode that illustrates precisely why a junior engineer's first substantive site duty is to verify, with disciplined rigour, that each connection is transmitting as designed.
